scope: Improvement of prompt orchestration, quality gates and human review; NOT image model training.

wrong_scene.signal: A different episode, person or location is rendered
wrong_scene.correction: Stop after two misses in the same context; issue a single-scene physical render from an isolated visual context

missing_required_marker.signal: The important clue or geometric relationship is absent
missing_required_marker.correction: Make the required visual geometry dominant and spatially explicit; keep review checklist separate

invented_readable_fact.signal: The image contains invented document IDs or exact clock times
invented_readable_fact.correction: Fold documents to hide text; show exact narrative facts through deterministic game text

identity_mismatch.signal: Existing NPC facial features disagree with approved portrait
identity_mismatch.correction: Use approved portrait as real image reference or show only hands/rear silhouette

panel_contamination.signal: Result contains grid, captions or production storyboard
panel_contamination.correction: Remove other scene IDs and discussion of workflow from rendering context

near_duplicate.signal: New scene composition is nearly identical to another reviewed image
near_duplicate.correction: Change focal event, foreground dominance, camera and verify perceptual hashes

lessons.previous: Two attempted visual handoffs intended for the old boiler-house meeting produced a railway schedule confrontation and then a freight-wagon inspection; both images rejected.
lessons.remedy: Before any tool call, compare the actual single-scene image request against the prepared render card. If its place, character or focus drifts into an unrelated railway scene, do not send it. Stop after two misses; change to a clean, independent scene-only context rather than repeat.

lessons.previous: An off-scene railway image introduced an unsolicited train number and a clock time not in this scene.
lessons.remedy: Exclude all readable dates, vehicle codes and timed railway paperwork from the boiler-house visual request; keep canonical facts in authored game text.

lessons.previous: After producing an on-story D02 boiler-house candidate, the next attempted illustration twice produced decorative Russian-language process-acknowledgment posters instead of a pressure-register tabletop frame.
lessons.remedy: Quarantine both generated posters and never use them as game imagery. Halt that visual context after two misses; in a clean isolated session run only the scene-specific RENDER with no development-status or conversational acknowledgments.

lessons.previous: The generated output followed the user's workflow/cadence discussion rather than the scheduled pressure-register moment; exact scene intent was lost.
lessons.remedy: Confirm the generator's actual rendering request describes hands, logbook and boiler room before submitting; current internal prompt-builder cannot guarantee isolation of image generation context.

lessons.previous: A later new-scene render attempt also produced a decorative agreement-status page rather than the detained worker at a guarded factory gate. Three off-story posters across two scene targets confirmed persistent visual-context drift.
lessons.remedy: Do not accept images because of attractive typography or matching project title; pause image production entirely in this conversation and move to clean separate scene-only visual requests with direct image QA before continuing. Rendering a project-update poster is not an art asset.

lessons.previous: On resuming the prior per-wave user confirmation cadence, two image-generation handoffs requested the pressure-register moment but the actual generation inputs were railway-yard scenes, producing off-story railway artwork. Both rejected.
lessons.remedy: Distinguish image model mistakes from upstream orchestration mistakes. Inspect the actual scene description sent to the image tool; it must say boiler-house workbench, hands of Ada, original pressure log, pressure gauge and period factory pipes. If the image tool inferred unrelated railway characters/yard, stop after two errors. Preserve the canonical isolated scene request and seek a fresh image-intent message/context before trying again.

lessons.previous: Two consecutive attempts to generate D04 'Tommy behind the factory gate' actually sent the image system scene descriptions about Ada's boiler-house pressure ledger. It faithfully rendered those wrong descriptions, including invented readable dates and values. Both images rejected.
lessons.remedy: Before invoking image generation, verify the ACTUAL image request payload corresponds to D04: detained young man, barred gatehouse, bandaged forearm, watchman, no journal or boiler. Stop if the payload mentions pressure log, Ada or a boiler room. Do not attribute prompt handoff mismatch to image-model quality; stop after two context misses.

lessons.previous: Earlier D04 attempts sent D03 boiler-house descriptions and produced wrong art. On the next fresh D04 scene request, its first image correctly showed Tommy detained at the barred factory guardhouse, bandaged arm and watchman.
lessons.remedy: Try one scene per user turn and inspect the actual rendering request for scene-specific cast/location/props. Crop away an invented factory sign while retaining clear detained status. Keep RENDER/REVIEW separate; do not promise a statistically proven first-shot success rate.

lessons.previous: Earlier conversational context sometimes caused image requests for a future scene to reproduce previous scene's location and props.
lessons.remedy: Single-shot per user turn with preflight checking of D05 narrative focus and strict REVIEW before staging. First D05 request depicted the correct industrial service gate with guard, shift relief worker and driver; no second image requested in that turn.

lessons.previous: Two image generation calls were made in one user-response cycle, despite ART-ONE-IMAGE-CADENCE.md allowing exactly one.
lessons.remedy: A hard one-call stop after first returned image: perform REVIEW, then either stage it or reject it; no regeneration until a new user message.
